definitions.gloss: letter; written document; formal written communication
definitions.explanation: A formal or official written communication, especially a letter. Often used in historical or formal contexts, as well as in legal and diplomatic settings.

examples.japanese: {抗議|こうぎ}の{書状|しょじょう}を{送|おく}る。
examples.english: To send a letter of protest.

examples.japanese: {大統領|だいとうりょう}から{書状|しょじょう}が{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: A letter arrived from the president.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}に{戦国時代|せんごくじだい}の{武将|ぶしょう}が{書|か}いた{書状|しょじょう}が{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: A letter written by a warlord from the Sengoku period is on display at the museum.

notes:
Composed of {書|しょ} (writing, document) + {状|じょう} (form, letter). A formal word for written correspondence, contrasting with the everyday word {手紙|てがみ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書状|しょじょう}を{送|おく}る: to send a letter
- {抗議|こうぎ}の{書状|しょじょう}: letter of protest
- {公開|こうかい}{書状|しょじょう}: open letter
- {書状|しょじょう}を{認|したた}める: to pen a letter (literary)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手紙|てがみ}: letter — the everyday word for a letter; informal and neutral
- {書簡|しょかん}: correspondence, letter — equally formal; used in literary and academic contexts
- {文書|ぶんしょ}: document, written text — broader; covers official documents, not just letters
- {親書|しんしょ}: personal letter (from a head of state) — specifically a diplomatic letter between leaders

USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in historical, legal, and diplomatic contexts. In everyday life, {手紙|てがみ} is the normal word for a letter. {書状|しょじょう} adds formality and gravity, suggesting an important or official communication.
